newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-ROMA SEND FOR VETERAN COACH NILS LIEDHOLM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROMA SEND FOR VETERAN COACH NILS LIEDHOLM.

text.p: Nils Liedholm, the grand old man of Italian soccer, was brought out of retirement on Tuesday by Roma as they bid to qualify for next season's UEFA Cup.
The shock appointment of the silver-haired Swede, his fourth spell in charge of Roma, came after Argentine Carlos Bianchi was sacked.
Bianchi was given his marching orders after Roma, lying seventh in the league, were beaten 2-1 by third-from-bottom Cagliari.
The Argentine was the sixth Serie A coach to lose his job this season.
Liedhold, 72, distinguished himself as a player with AC Milan in the 1950s and 1960s before embarking on a glittering career as a coach.
Nicknamed "The Baron", he has been retired since 1992 when he left his job as Verona coach.

Italian sports newspapers said that Liedholm -- in charge when Roma last won the championship in 1983 -- was a temporary solution and that the club had their eyes on veteran Giovanni Trapattoni, currently at the helm of Bayern Munich.
